html:
Unreal asset property operations

ForgeMCP exposes bounded inspection and reviewed in-memory edits for assets under /Game and /JasperPrism. These operations run on the Unreal Editor game thread. Loading the selected asset may load its normal dependencies. ForgeMCP does not walk object references or inspect container contents through these commands.

Inspect

unreal_inspect_asset_properties returns simple reflected values for one exact asset: booleans, numeric values, enums, names, bounded strings and display text, FVector, FRotator, FLinearColor, and FColor. Each value includes its reflected C++ type and editor editability flag. Complex structs, arrays, maps, sets, object references, transient fields, and fixed arrays are omitted and counted. Results are limited to 200 entries; integer values are decimal strings so 64-bit values remain exact.

Review and apply one edit

unreal_preview_asset_property_edit takes an exact asset path, reflected property name, and a value string in Unreal's native property text syntax. The property must be a single editable instance property of a supported type. The native adapter parses the proposed value using the selected property's own FProperty, rejects non-finite numeric/vector/color values, and returns normalized current and proposed values.

Example:

{
  "session_id": "[redacted]",
  "request": {
    "asset_path": "/Game/Props/SM_Rock.SM_Rock",
    "property_name": "LightMapResolution",
    "property_value": "128"
  }
}

Pass the returned preview_id as both preview_id and confirmation to unreal_apply_asset_property_edit. The preview expires after five minutes and is single-use. It binds the loaded object identity, class, property and current value. Apply rejects stale previews, dirty packages, properties that are no longer editable, and assets that cannot participate in an Unreal editor transaction. The apply enables RF_Transactional on the loaded object when needed, records an Editor transaction, sets the property, calls Unreal's edit notifications, and verifies the normalized result. The transaction flag remains on that loaded object. The adapter reports that it recorded a transaction; interactive Undo behavior is a separate acceptance check.

The command changes memory only and reports package_dirty: true and saved: false. It never saves or overwrites the asset package. Inspect the result, then save through the Editor when the user authorizes persistence. Saving, disk backups, complex property editing, object-reference assignment, and batch edits are not implemented.

The property acceptance fixture uses a disposable UE 5.6.1 project and real MCP stdio. It verifies a StaticMesh integer edit, reinspection, native transaction tracking, invalid and non-finite values, confirmation, replay, stale-preview and dirty-package rejection. The user's JasperPrism project was not used for mutation.
